title: Self-healing playbook: automated remediation for common Private deployment health failures
creator: Ana Patel
description: Create a runnable, testable runbook and automated remediation playbooks for the most common Private (VPC) deployment health check failures. The goal is twofold: 1) provide concise operator runbooks for on-call to triage and remediate incidents quickly, 2) implement safe automated remediation hooks (operator-controlled) that can perform non-destructive fixes (terraform drift apply, config reconcile, rolling restarts, certificate reissue) and escalate when human approval is required. This ticket covers discovery of failure modes, runbook authoring, Terraform/IaC reconciliation recipes, circuit-breaker policies, and integration tests against a staging Private deployment. Excludes full redesign of health checks — focuses on remediation and orchestration for currently deployed checks.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Operator-facing runbook (short form) exists for top 6 failure classes and is validated by SRE + Private eng
A2: Automated remediation playbooks implemented as orchestrator jobs (k8s Job or controller) for 4 safe actions with rollback and rate limits
A3: Terraform module 'private-reconcile' and example usage documented and tested in staging to fix common drift scenarios
A4: Alerts updated to include remediation confidence and a toggle to enable/disable automation per-customer
A5: End-to-end smoke tests that intentionally induce each failure in staging and verify remediation or escalation behavior
steps_runbook: Overview: When a Private instance reports unhealthy via 'private-agent-heartbeat' or 'private-health-check' channel, follow triage -> attempt safe remediation -> monitor -> escalate if unresolved.

Triage: Check Redwood Console > Private > <customer> > Instances for error type and recent events. Open associated Grafana dashboard (link in Links) and copy relevant traces/metrics into the incident chat.

Step 1 - heartbeat-missing: check agent process on host via SSH (systemd status: 'sudo systemctl status redwood-agent'). If inactive, run 'sudo journalctl -u redwood-agent -n 200' then 'sudo systemctl restart redwood-agent' and monitor for heartbeat for 2 minutes.

Step 2 - cert-rotation-failure: inspect '/etc/redwood/agent/certs' and validate commonName and expiry with 'openssl x509 -in agent.crt -noout -dates'. For manual reissue use the 'private-cert-rotate' script: '/opt/redwood/bin/rotate-agent-cert --env staging --instance <id>' then restart agent.

Step 3 - terraform-drift-detected (network/security-group): run 'terraform -chdir=iac/private plan -var='instance=<id>' -out=tfplan' and review diffs. If changes are wanted, run 'terraform apply tfplan' under on-call approval. For automated remediation, see remediation_playbooks entry 'tf-reconcile-job'.

Step 4 - nginx-proxy-503 / tcp-proxy failover: validate backend connectivity 'curl -v --max-time 5 http://127.0.0.1:8080/health'. If backend fails, trigger rolling restart of service group: '/opt/redwood/bin/rolling-restart --service proxy --group <group-id>' to drain and reattach backends.

Step 5 - kv-cache-corruption / storage errors: place instance into maintenance mode via Console, run 'redwood-toolbox kv-check --fix --instance <id>' which runs checksum/repair. If repair fails, snapshot logs and escalate to Storage team (tag storage-eng).

Step 6 - routing/dns issues (Route53/Cloud DNS): verify DNS resolve from within VPC 'dig +short @<customer-dns> service.private.redwood.internal'. If mismatch, inspect Terraform records under 'iac/dns' and follow tf reconcile steps; if automated, create DNS reconcile change with 'dns-reconcile' job (see remediation_playbooks).
Escalation: If automated actions fail or service remains degraded for >15 minutes, mark incident 'Escalate' and page Private Eng rotation. Attach logs and list remediation steps attempted.
remediation_playbooks: tf-reconcile-job: k8s Job that clones infrastructure repo, runs 'terraform init && terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply -auto-approve tfplan' in read-only mode for drift detection, but only applies changes that match an allowlist (security groups, DNS, tags). Job returns a JSON summary to the incident channel. Configurable via Customer customData tags and operator flag.

agent-restart-controller: controller that performs a coordinated restart across an instance group with per-instance health probes and backoff (max 3 restarts per 10 minutes). If restarts exceed threshold, controller opens a manual approval gate to prevent crash loops.

cert-rotate-automation: Lambda/k8s job that attempts to reissue agent certs using customer's KMS keys and the Redwood CA service. The job runs in 'dry-run' mode by default; on operator approval ('approve-rotate' label) it performs the rotation and restarts agents.

dns-failover-reconciler: automated reconciler that validates expected ingress endpoints and reconciles Route53 records via Terraform provider only when TTL < 60s and reconciliation confidence score >= 0.8. Falls back to fail-open state (no change) if provider API errors are encountered.

kv-repair-orchestrator: runbook-triggered job that verifies snapshot integrity, creates a fresh cache instance, and swaps traffic via feature-flagged router. Includes automatic rollback if post-swap health check fails within 3 minutes.
tests_and_validation: Staging harness: terraform staging instance builder that can inject failure modes (stop agent, corrupt cert, alter SG). Use it to run the smoke tests.
E2E smoke tests: pipeline job 'ci/private-remediate' that performs each failure simulation and asserts remediation succeeds or escalates correctly.
Chaos window: schedule a supervised chaos run with SRE + Private Eng where automated remediation toggles are exercised at 2am-4am PT with an on-call present.
Rollback tests: simulate a misapplied terraform change and validate policies (allowlist, rate limit) prevent wide blast radius and that operator rollback works.
